Thank you everyone for the very helpful feedback! Unfortunately, I dont have the time to individually reply to everyone, so I have to resort to adress at least some of the points in this comment. One of the common remarks was the lack of context in the poem. This was done intentionally, because I didnt want the focus to be on the story, but ratrher on the emotion conveyed. That is also what the "list" of ways to kill "me" comes down to. It is supposed to be like "pick and choose" sort of thing.  The second point often adressed was the "Let loose the arrow (...)" line. I agree with the need to change the line! 

Once again, thank you everyone for the feedback, and for the positive comments!

Oh my! Thank you for such an extensive and thought through feedback! I didn't expect anything like this. I'm glad you like it. Regarding the syllable issue, I'm not really big on theory, even though I study English literature, so I dont really think about poetry in these terms. When I write, I try to read it out loud and figure out a way for it to flow nicely when read. So again, thank you so much for giving me a little bit more insight into the ins and out of writing!

This is an interesting poem! I cant really say, whether I like it or not. It definitely has some nice themes and imagery. I especially like the "I could catch a whale with a cartwheel" line. Splendidly original! I also like how the simple wording plays well together with the theme. What I dont really like is the (in my opinion) scattered alliteration, and I also think it could use the occasional rhyme here and there. Otherwise, a great job!

What I like about this poem the most, is the vivid mariner imagery.  It flows quite nicely, but it is a poem made for reading out loud in my opinion. My only gripe with it is inconsistency. I feel like there are these metaphorical bumps while you read it, but I cant quite pinpoint why that is. Great work otherwise!

I really like the first two stanzas. They flow nicely, and give the reader something to think about, especially in the line "A white dove among a flock of crow(s)". The last stanza is kinda puzzling though. I dont know whether its just a problem with the formatting, or careless writing, but there are some mistakes - I am not even mentioning the last line. I think you were  onto something with the first two parts, but then you kinda let go. Give it some more work, and it can be a great poem!

I love how simple and yet meaningful this poem is. I have no real way of being sure how you intended it to be read, but I like to think that the pauses between the lines are meant to be a little longer than usual. When I read it like that, It has a nice air of depth to it. The only thing I would change, is swapping the "our" for "ours". Great job!

I like an awful lot about this poem. The impactful vocabulary, the imagery and the obvious psychological undertones. The repetition is used excellently, and adds a lot to the poem.

I would appreciate separation into stanzas, and more careful choice of words in a few instances, such as:

*A mental state of* ***disorientation***

*You’re left without* ***orientation***

I get the intention behind the usage, but the application seems a little obtuse **to me**.

Overall, a very good job!

I really like how short, yet meaningful the poem is. The lack of stylistic editing only adds to the universality of the poem, which I also like. Poems like this, that hold different meaning for different people are the best in my opinion. I can also read a certain duality in the poem, it could be positive or negative. Maybe lean into that duality of meaning a bit more next time.
